messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming tail latency spike detected on prod-region-eu (route: /v1/stream). Affected: SSE + websocket streams showing >30s gaps (observed silence). paging oncall @maya :rotating_light:
maya: I’m on it. grabbing context now — which customers?
lucy-support: support: getting customer reports — two enterprise tenants reported long pauses and reconnects, flagged as partial degradation.
alex: seeing burst of 520s from proxy layer followed by client disconnects in the logs. p95 up ~600ms -> p99 > 18s.
ravi: attaching quick grep of edge proxy logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:12:01Z proxy[upstream-45] INFO stream: write 124b to client
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z proxy[upstream-45] WARN tcp: connection stalled, tx-buffer=0, rx-window=0
2026-03-15T14:12:33Z proxy[upstream-47] ERROR write timeout after 30s
```
jen-sre: interesting — timeouts clustered on a subset of proxy instances (eu-proxy-4, eu-proxy-7). Could be keepalive/epoll backlog or TLS renegotiation issue.
maya: steps: 1) identify if it’s infra or client backpressure 2) mitigate to restore streams 3) collect traces for root cause.
alex: I’m tailing the streaming controller metrics: continuous-batch wait times spike correlating with proxy timeouts. `kv-cache-hit` unaffected.
ravi: checking kernel sock stats on eu-proxy-7: `netstat -tan | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l` high but not exhausted. however `ss -s` shows retransmits and some memory pressure.
lucy-support: customer-impact note: two tenants (acct-1982, acct-5543) saw ~40% stream failures; others partial. raising to SE leads.
maya: mitigation idea: move traffic off eu-proxy-7 and eu-proxy-4, drain them, and roll back the recent proxy sidecar config that enabled aggressive `tcp_quickack` changes deployed ~14:00 UTC. alex, can you start a canary reroute?
alex: can do. creating temporary upstream weight shift via LB: `svc/upstream-eu weight: set eu-proxy-7=0, eu-proxy-4=0` — kicking now.
incident-bot: @maya annotated: runbook -> streaming-silence -> step 3 (drain suspected proxies).
jen-sre: also recommend bumping proxy keepalive to 60s and disable `enable_tcp_nodelay` toggle from the 14:00 patch as quick rollback.
ravi: I can ssh and apply sysctl tweak to increase `tcp_max_syn_backlog` and bump `somaxconn` on those nodes while traffic is drained.
alex: reroute applied. traffic now avoided eu-proxy-4/7. new tail latency graphs show p99 dropping from ~18s -> ~2.2s within 40s.
lucy-support: customers reporting streams recover (acct-1982 confirms partial recovery). sending update to SEs. :white_check_mark:
maya: good. collect heap/profile on the drained nodes before restart. jen, can you run a `tcpdump` capture for 60s to capture silent periods?
jen-sre: running capture now: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/sse-silence-eu4.pcap port 443 and host 10.2.45.7`
incident-bot: TIMELINE NOTE: detection 14:12 UTC, mitigation (reroute) 14:15 UTC, notable recovery 14:16-14:17 UTC.
alex: we should revoke the 14:00 proxy feature flag entirely until we confirm. I’ll open a rollback PR.
ravi: on eu-proxy-7 I see a lot of `SSL_read` stalls where worker threads are stuck reading from socket buffer for >25s (blocked syscalls). suspecting a libssl renegotiation edge-case with our custom TLS session ticket rotation.
maya: tagged eng-runtime (cc: @alex) — please investigate TLS rotation code path. For now keep eu-proxy-4/7 drained and schedule restart during this window.
lucy-support: updating customers with root cause (investigating TLS rotation) and mitigation (traffic reroute + restart).
jen-sre: capture saved. uploading to incident channel artifacts.
maya: handoff to night oncall @jen-sre in 45m. We have traffic routed away, p99 stabilized but still above baseline. Action items for handoff:
- keep eu-proxy-4/7 drained and restart one at a time after collecting perf traces
- revert proxy sidecar TLS rotation flag and redeploy canary
- correlate TLS ticket rotation times with observed stalls from traces
- customer comms draft ready (lucy)
jen-sre: acknowledged. I’ll monitor for next 2 hours and run sa-cluster restart on eu-proxy-7 after trace collection.
alex: opened rollback PR #6123 and set CI hold.
lucy-support: comms: "We observed partial streaming interruptions due to edge TLS session rotation interactions with our proxy. We mitigated by rerouting traffic and restarting affected proxies. Engineers are continuing investigation and will follow up with RCA." Sending to SEs now.
maya: prep follow-up incident ticket and RCA once eng-runtime confirms root cause. For now: pages cleared? Set status to partial-degradation -> mitigation-in-progress.
incident-bot: Incident status updated -> mitigation-in-progress. severity set to sev2.
jen-sre: quick note for handoff: p95 at 400-600ms, p99 at ~2s currently; keeping a close eye. leaving active watch for ~90m. I’ll escalate if residual >5% error rate.
maya: thanks team. handing off to @jen-sre. If any customer escalations, page SRE rotation and ENG-runtime lead.
jen-sre: taking it. will post updates in this thread. leaving final note: don’t re-enable TLS ticket rotation flag until we have validated fix.
